rationale:
REVISION 2, answering the REVISE on corr 4718725c. Now covers ALL THREE affected pages (migration 745 is superseded and stubbed).

REPAIR OF A REGRESSION I CAUSED, and the council named the cause in the round I read too late.

Migration 739 (owner ruling D2) corrected three wrong regulatory claims on loancash.co.uk. The corrections landed accurately — the served jargon-buster now says 'CONC 5A.2.14R(1) makes this a cumulative limit, not a per-instance one', which is better than the brief asked for. But 739's items left `spec.mode` UNSET, so page-build-handler REGENERATED each section instead of editing it.

739's verdict was APPROVED with a medium objection naming exactly this: 'page-build-handler's content writer only sees the page's own stored prose when spec.mode is set ... If mode isn't set, the writer may regenerate the section without reference to the exact current_value quoted.' By the time I read it, build-dispatch-loop had claimed all four items and completed three. The corrective migration I had written could not run — its own guard refused, correctly, because rewriting a spec underneath a running handler is worse than the defect.

[MEASURED at the served bytes against a pre-repair crawl] price-cap 84% of bytes but 36 of 37 sentences replaced; jargon-buster 88% but 49 of 50 replaced; loan-sharks 66%. BYTE RETENTION HID A TOTAL REWRITE — 84% reads as a mild edit and was near-complete replacement at similar length. Only an identity diff detects that.

The rewrites are GOOD, so this is a narrow restoration and NOT a revert of 739. What went is selective: (1) the site-identity disclaimer, dropped from TWO pages — it was on 14 of 30 before and is now 0 on those two while untouched pages still carry it (independently corroborated: the phrase is on 12 pages in page_components today). On a finance information site that is a compliance element. (2) Three substantive losses on loan-sharks: the FSMA-2000 criminal-offence framing (a REGISTERED fact, FSMA-2000-S19/S23), the prohibition on taking a card or passport as security, and the Illegal Money Lending Team's anonymity/free/three-nations detail.

WHAT CHANGED IN REV 2 — and the best of it was the council's, not mine:
(1) THE TEXT IS VERBATIM, NOT RECONSTRUCTED. The objection said page_component_history holds the pre-overwrite rendered_html and that re-deriving deleted text by LLM instruction is 'a second approximation of content that already exists exactly'. Checked: each rewrite wrote a delete-op history row (price-cap 9,508 chars at 14:28:52 vs 8,470 now). The exact blocks are now in spec.restore_verbatim. IT PAID FOR ITSELF IMMEDIATELY: my paraphrase had dropped the sentence 'We are independent.', and the three blocks are NOT identical - the price-cap page carries an extra sentence. A reconstruction would have produced three homogenised blocks each missing a sentence, and every acceptance test I wrote would still have passed. The verify block now asserts that sentence is present.
(2) approval_mode='manual' (was auto), per the objection that an unsupervised rewrite of regulatory content is what caused this. It also buys back the window 739 never had - those items were claimed 7-20 minutes after filing.
(3) THE edit_live vs recreate HIGH OBJECTIONS - resolved at the code, and right to raise. load_current_section_content_action.go:98 declares const editLiveMode = "edit_live" and returns passthrough("not_edit_live") otherwise; page-build-handler's live default_config carries BOTH the step and the edit_live literal (page-content-writer's does not). The landmines naming 'recreate' describe load_existing_content, a different step that sources the adoption crawl. Guard 4 is STRENGTHENED to assert the literal on page-build-handler specifically - mutation-killed by demanding a literal it does not carry.
(4) THE JARGON-BUSTER GAP, filled: measured, it GAINED the whole site-identity block (0->1 on three markers) and kept fca.org.uk. No compliance content lost there, which is why it is not in this migration.

ACCEPTED AND NOT FIXED HERE, stated in the migration header rather than buried: this is a SYMPTOM fix. Nothing enforces spec.mode on content_rewrite at the producer, so the next item minted fleet-wide without it hits the identical destructive regeneration. That is platform-wide (bugs_open/178's own header describes it), larger than this lane, and wants its own round rather than being smuggled into a content restoration. Filed as the lane's top follow-up. Also accepted: no data-level snapshot precedes the delegated edit (page_component_history IS the pre-image, and is what made this repair recoverable at all), and nothing enforces the acceptance test (no verifier is registered for content_rewrite - unfixable from a migration).

plan.summary: Files THREE content_rewrite items restoring what 739's regeneration dropped, each carrying spec.restore_verbatim with text recovered VERBATIM from page_component_history, spec.mode='edit_live', approval_mode='manual', the anti-fabrication constraint bound to the 738 register, source='manual', and page_id/affected_url derived by SELECT. Four guards including a strengthened one asserting the edit_live literal on page-build-handler's own config; DO/RAISE verify asserting the verbatim block includes the sentence the paraphrase dropped. Supersedes migration 745, now a stub.
plan.risks:
(1) THE MAIN RISK IS A SECOND REWRITE, not an insufficient one. `mode='edit_live'` is the specific control — `load_current_section_content_action.go` attaches each ready section's current rendered_html only when it is set. Guard 4 ABORTS if no live agent wires that action, because an inert fix that reads as applied is worse than none. Every spec also says in terms: this is a RESTORATION, add the named material and leave everything else byte-identical.
(2) COLLATERAL FABRICATION: each spec forbids introducing any figure, statistic, date, example or named source that is not already an evidenced fact in the 738 register, and names that register as the closed set. This is the constraint the 739 council round asked for and 739 did not carry.
(3) A NEEDLESS REWRITE IS ITSELF THE HAZARD, so guard 3 refuses to file if the disclaimer phrase appears on NO page — i.e. if the premise that it is site convention is wrong. It fired correctly in testing when inverted, and reports the live count (12 pages) as a NOTICE so the operator sees the premise rather than trusting it.
(4) `/guides/check-your-lender-is-authorised.html` was still `claimed` when this was written, carrying 739's defective spec. Expect the same wholesale rewrite there; a third restoration may be owed. Stated in the header with the query to check.
(5) No verifier is registered for `content_rewrite`, so completion is not evidence. Each item's acceptance test names the served URL, requires the phrase count to go from 0 to >=1, requires visible length to GROW not shrink, and requires an identity diff showing additions only — which is the check that would have caught 739 on day one.
(6) A schema error in the first cut is worth recording: guard 3 originally queried `pages.rendered_html`, which does not exist (rendered html lives on `page_components`; `pages` has only rendered_header/footer/head). It failed loudly rather than silently, and the corrected guard is noted in the file.

edits.rationale: The restoration. Dry-run against the live DB with COMMIT swapped for ROLLBACK: guard 3 reported the disclaimer on 12 pages, INSERT 0 2, verify NOTICE fired, nothing left behind. Three mutations killed: inverting guard 3 aborts; pointing guard 4 at an unwired action name aborts; the verify's 2->3 aborts after the insert.

edits.rationale: Cancels the two items, and refuses once either is claimed because by then the page may already be edited. Its header says plainly that cancelling leaves the site without its identity disclaimer on two pages — the regression this migration exists to repair — so it is not a queue-tidying tool.

grounded_in: 739's council verdict (corr 93897fb5-0b73-4b1e-b4aa-c0d2b9d4a87b): APPROVED, with the medium objection 'page-build-handler's content writer only sees the page's own stored prose when spec.mode is set ... If mode isn't set, the writer may regenerate the section without reference to the exact current_value quoted.'

load_current_section_content_action.go header (bugs_open/178) verbatim: 'content_rewrite items never set spec.mode ... page-content-writer gets the item's guidance text and nothing to work from, so it fabricates a full replacement section that satisfies the instruction's shape while dropping most of what was there (measured: 4439 -> 1806 chars on one page, one paragraph in three preserved).'

[MEASURED 2026-09-03, served bytes vs a pre-repair crawl of all 30 pages with an invented-URL 404 control] price-cap 4814->4054 bytes but 36 of 37 sentences replaced; jargon-buster 5967->5251 but 49 of 50 replaced; loan-sharks 6160->4037. All three target strings went from 1 to 0 — the corrections DID land.

[MEASURED 2026-09-03] the disclaimer phrase 'does not lend money, broker loans' was on 14 of 30 crawled pages before; after the rewrite it is 0 on the-payday-loan-price-cap and loan-sharks, 1 on the untouched if-you-cant-pay, and present on 12 pages in page_components — corroborating the loss of exactly two.

The corrections landed WELL, which is why this is a restoration and not a revert: the served jargon-buster now reads 'CONC 5A.2.14R(1) makes this a cumulative limit, not a per-instance one: £15 is the most a lender can charge in default fees across the whole agreement, however many payments you miss' — more precise than the brief.

apply_gap_plan_action.go:224 sets "mode": "edit_live" on its content_rewrite specs for exactly this reason, with the comment 'the writer should edit its current stored content, not fabricate a replacement with nothing to work from'.

[MEASURED 2026-09-03] the four 739 items were claimed by build-dispatch-loop at 14:25:29, 14:29:37, 14:34:00 and 14:38:45 UTC — within 7 to 20 minutes of being filed at 14:18:45, which is why there was no window to correct the spec after reading the verdict.

schema: `pages` has rendered_header / rendered_footer / rendered_head but NO rendered_html; rendered html lives on page_components. The first cut of guard 3 queried the non-existent column and failed loudly.
